races.name: William Hill Silver Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Theoryofeverything
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for O'Meara who has been busy on good ground all season; similar-going form reads 1W2P from six starts which is encouraging, but the step up to genuinely heavy going at Beverley represents an untested variable and the closing style may find the pace insufficient to generate a winning run.
runners_data.comment: Theoryofeverything arrives in fine heart on the back of a win last time out, has experience over today's trip and going, and his rating of 98 marks him as a serious threat here; the risk is that his record in recent starts shows inconsistency outside that latest victory.

runners_data.name: Impartiality
runners_data.note: Shane Gray partners this prominent racer who has placed twice from six similar-going runs; drops slightly in trip compared to recent outings but the style suits this race shape perfectly — tracking Amancio and delivering from two out is exactly the scenario this race creates.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in his last two starts, Impartiality arrives here fit on a 19-day turnaround with experience of both today's trip and going, and his rating of 93 makes him a strong case despite being yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Jake Dickson claims five pounds on this hold-up horse whose similar-going record is thin (2 from 15, 0W1P); the step up to 1m2f is a positive given the 12f placed efforts in the formbook, but Tim Easterby's yard is firing (4/71 in 14 days) and the horse needs a stronger pace than Amancio is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts yet Wahdan's third two runs back signals a resurgence in form, and carrying 137 lb from stall five he shapes as a lively threat with his rating of 94 suggesting he is better than his official mark; the risk is that he must prove that latest fourth represented genuine progress.

runners_data.name: Tiger
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose recent form over 10-12f on soft and good-to-soft is strong — a win and two seconds — making him one of the more credible closers if the heavy ground creates a sufficiently searching test; Paul Mulrennan is an astute partner but the controlled tempo is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of his last three starts, including a win two starts back, Tiger arrives on a sound 22-day break with distance and going experience to call on, though ranked seventh of thirteen he faces a stiff ask at 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Rhys Elliott (5lb claim) partners this prominent racer in good form — a win and a second in last four starts — though similar-going data is sparse at 1 from 15; Sam England's yard is in reasonable touch and the style suits a race where the pace positions directly behind Amancio are there to be claimed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift on our figures in a field of 13, Jez Bomb is hard to fancy off 135 lb despite a decent recent record that includes a winner two starts back and a second three starts back in his last six.

runners_data.name: Fox Avatar
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald rides for Roger Varian (5/17 in 14 days, yard in form) and this prominent type won over 12f on Tapeta, suggesting stamina is not a concern; however, just one similar-going run from eleven with no wins or places is a flag on heavy ground, and the lack of soft/heavy form is the key risk.
runners_data.comment: Fox Avatar won four starts back but has since gone third, seventh, and sixth in recent starts, form that is hard to ignore on the negative side; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough, though the 135 lb burden is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Kind Of Kiss
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse wearing a tongue-tie, 41 days off the track, and whose similar-going record offers only one place from three starts; Sam England trains and the horse is likely to need a stronger pace to be involved — the controlled Amancio tempo is unfavourable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kind Of Kiss has nonetheless run over today's trip and going conditions, and a our rating of 92 suggests considerably more ability than his official mark of 80 implies; the risk is that his recent finishes offer little encouragement of an imminent turnaround.

runners_data.name: Oratorical
runners_data.note: Laura Pearson takes the ride on this three-year-old who has the best heavy-ground form in the field — a win and a place from two starts on heavy — which stands out sharply; the 115-day layoff and the trainer's 0/12 in 14 days are negatives, but the genuine heavy-ground credentials make him one to respect in a true test.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last two starts and absent for 115 days, Oratorical is hard to fancy on these figures, ranked tenth of thirteen in the field; the win three starts back offers a glimmer, but fitness after a lengthy layoff is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Galyx
runners_data.note: George Bass partners this prominent type for Jack Channon (2/22 in 14 days); similar-going record is the best in the field numerically at 2W4P from six starts, though recent form has tailed off and the horse has placed rather than won at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Galyx at least showed a hint of promise with a third four starts back, though a sixth last time out and 132 lb from stall 12 make progress hard to envisage, despite having distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, fresh from a 63-day break, wearing a tongue-tie, with two wins and three places from eight similar-going starts; Tom Eaves rides for Faye Bramley and the horse has proven ability on soft — the unchallenged lead here is a significant tactical asset on heavy going.
runners_data.comment: Amancio won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, solid claims; however, he has not run for 63 days and carries 131 lb from stall 13, question marks that could blunt his chance at a competitive weight.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural style has placed him in a midfield map position because of the volume of similar types in the field — his similar-going record is 0W0P from two runs, and he is the most likely to be disadvantaged by racing out of his instinctive position; David Allan rides for Tim Easterby.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Per Contra's best recent effort was a fourth two starts back, though an eighth last time out is the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 130 lb from stall seven, and rates higher than his official mark suggests.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Myths
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with just two runs — a win and a third on good — bringing freshness and upside but also profound uncertainty; a natural prominent racer who may struggle to secure that position in a competitive 13-runner field, and the complete absence of soft or heavy ground form is a significant unknown.
runners_data.comment: Bay Of Myths won two starts back but has been off the track for 132 days, and our figures rank him near the foot of the field; he has run over today's trip, but fitness after such a lengthy absence is the real concern here.

runners_data.name: Mudita
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's three-year-old was running just eight days ago and is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, placed in the midfield mapping because of the volume of hold-up types; Ethan Tindall claims five pounds but the horse has never encountered soft or heavy ground and that inexperience on this surface is a substantial query.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mudita has placed just twice in her last five starts, with only a single win in recent form, and she faces a stiff ask from stall 11 carrying 116 lb, though she has run over today's trip and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Amancio is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, critically, faces no direct pressure for the lead — he can bowl along at whatever tempo suits him on heavy ground at Beverley. With no rival willing or able to contest the early fractions, Amancio will dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a sapping pace duel, which on this ground could prove dangerously effective for a horse who has already won on soft. The prominent runners — Impartiality, Jez Bomb, Fox Avatar, Oratorical, and Galyx — will track him through the first half of the race, while the hold-up brigade must settle further back and hope the pace is sufficient to generate a true test. This shape, with one sole leader dictating a measured tempo on heavy going over a mile and two furlongs, strongly favours prominent racers who can settle just off the pace and pounce without needing a truly fierce gallop to be generated ahead of them. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all occupy their natural position: Bay Of Myths and Per Contra are genuine prominent and hold-up horses respectively who are mapped to midfield, and Mudita is a true hold-up type also mapped forward — of these, Bay Of Myths is best placed to recover something close to a natural position given youth and freshness, but the prominent positions directly behind Amancio are likely claimed by Impartiality, Jez Bomb, and Fox Avatar.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amancio Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Amancio leads unchallenged at a regulated pace and a prominent tracker delivers a clean challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Amancio sets a measured tempo on heavy ground, preserving energy while the prominent horses behind him idle in a tight group; as the field swings for home the best of those prominent trackers — unencumbered by ground-sapping pace war — has the fuel to pounce cleanly. Horses who have settled just off the pace without expending early energy are the primary beneficiaries, particularly those with proven stamina on this ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Them All
scenarios.trigger: If Amancio's controlled early fractions leave him with enough reserves to simply grind on relentlessly through the heavy ground and the chasers cannot sustain their effort.
scenarios.body: On a flat but stamina-sapping Beverley track in true heavy conditions, a relaxed front-runner who has dictated every yard can prove impossible to reel in if the chasers have depleted themselves merely keeping contact; Amancio has won on soft and his connections have freshened him up with a 63-day break. The hold-up horses most reliant on a fast tempo to get into the race would find this scenario especially punishing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If Amancio sets a fast enough honest gallop to string the field out and the genuine hold-up types can find the room to deliver a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Tiger is a genuine hold-up horse with a recent win over this trip on good-to-soft and a second on soft, and Theoryofeverything has similar closing credentials; if the pace is strong enough their finishing efforts can bring them into contention in the closing stages. However, with Amancio likely to manage the tempo conservatively, this scenario depends on conditions creating a more draining race than the lone front-runner is likely to manufacture.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Market Mover
scenarios.trigger: If the field splits tactically, pace judgement breaks down, or redistributed horses create unexpected positional traffic that disrupts the settled race shape.
scenarios.body: Bay Of Myths is a lightly raced three-year-old with natural prominent tendencies who could unsettle the established order if freshness sends them forward to press Amancio harder than anticipated; Per Contra or Mudita, displaced from their true hold-up roles, could find themselves caught in no-man's land and inadvertently disrupt the rhythm of those around them. In this fractured scenario the race becomes a test of adaptability and raw ability over class and tactics.

watchPoints.text: Oratorical's two heavy-ground runs produced a win and a place — if the going tests stamina as expected, watch whether Laura Pearson can slot him into a position close enough to Amancio to deliver his effort before the race is won.

Bay Of Myths is fresh, lightly raced, and a natural prominent type; watch the early stages to see whether Gina Mangan pushes forward to claim a position behind Amancio — if she does, it could disrupt the settled order the other prominent runners are counting on.

Fox Avatar's similar-going record (1 from 11, 0W0P) contrasts sharply with yard form — if PJ McDonald finds himself unable to travel as fluently as expected on heavy ground, the prominent position he needs to be effective may cost him in the finish.

Amancio's pace management in the first half-mile is the key variable for the entire race — if Tom Eaves sets only a dawdle, the hold-up horses will be entirely cut out of the contest and the race becomes a sprint between prominent horses; if he stretches them honestly, the closers get a chance.

Tiger and Theoryofeverything are the two most credible hold-up closers on form, but both need Amancio to run at a pace that genuinely tests the field — monitor whether the early sectionals suggest a stamina test or a tactical dawdle that renders their finishing kicks redundant.

races.name: William Hill Beverley Bullet Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Washington Heights
runners_data.note: An on-pace six-year-old who handles soft conditions adequately (3 runs, 0W1P in similar going) and is primed off a 21-day break for Kevin Ryan with Tom Eaves up; races prominently which is exactly the position to be in today given the single-pace-setter scenario.
runners_data.comment: Washington Heights arrives here on the back of a lively effort last time out, finishing second 21 days ago, and he won three starts back, making him a genuine threat with experience over today's trip and going; the main concern is that eighth two starts back suggests some inconsistency to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ain't Nobody
runners_data.note: True hold-up type fitted with a hood, just nine days since last run, and his one heavy-ground start produced a seventh — his natural style leaves him needing a pace collapse that the field shape makes unlikely today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ain't Nobody at least brings experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 114 puts him narrowly top on our figures; the 130 lb burden is the one note of caution, but he merits respect from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Al Shabab Storm
runners_data.note: Returned a winner on his most recent outing but that was on a standard surface, and while his prominent instincts are genuine, the overcrowded position near the pace means he is likely to find himself in midfield against his wishes, softening his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but has been unplaced in two of his three starts before that, and 65 days off the track raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 130 lb from stall six, and an official mark of 102 keeps him competitive if straight enough to show that winning form.

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: A consistent front-rank performer with three wins in his last six — his natural inclination to race prominently is solid, but with so many rivals wanting the same ground he may not secure a comfortable pitch, and his sole heavy-going run produced no place evidence.
runners_data.comment: Landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back before filling the runner-up spot last time out, and he has distance and going experience in his favour, but a mark of 99 and 130 lb from stall 10 are testing conditions for a horse who was unplaced two starts back.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for the Quinn yard, fitted with a hood and nine days fresh; his front-running role is straightforward here, though his recent form string shows he has not won in several attempts and heavy going is uncharted territory for him.
runners_data.comment: Jm Jungle shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns here in fine order just nine days on, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour at 130 lb from stall nine; the concern is he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Shagraan
runners_data.note: Clive Cox five-year-old off a 57-day break with P J McDonald; won on soft at Beverley and has course and going credentials that matter — prominent style suits the race shape perfectly and the layoff combined with the step back to manageable handicap weights gives him each-way claims.
runners_data.comment: Shagraan shaped with promise when third four starts back and went one better to score five starts back, and he arrives here with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; the concern is that he has been off for 57 days and returns to action carrying 130 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Argentine Tango
runners_data.note: Won on soft as a three-year-old and has prominent instincts, but with several older rivals competing for the same early positions this lightly-weighted youngster is liable to be pushed back from his natural berth, diluting his effectiveness on a track he has not visited.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back but unplaced on her most recent outing, Argentine Tango has experience of today's trip and going and returns after 30 days; the 126 lb burden is a concern, though her rating of 103 suggests she retains ability.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly fitted with a visor, off 33 days for Ben Haslam; best efforts have come over six furlongs and her lack of a win or place on similar going over five furlongs suggests today's combination of trip and ground is against her.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and without a win in her last three starts, Beaujolais Nouveau faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and arrives on a reasonable freshener of 33 days.

runners_data.name: Elegant Erin
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old hold-up performer with two wins in similar going across her last five runs — the most convincing closer in the field, though Beverley's flat straight offers little in the way of a stamina test to help her past rivals who have been able to settle near the pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and winless in her last six starts, Elegant Erin at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, though 58 days between runs and a speed rating of 83 make her a tough sell at the weights.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good ground but his heavy-going record is thin (0W0P in one run), and being pushed from his natural prominent position into midfield through redistribution reduces confidence in him running to his best RPR today.
runners_data.comment: Fluorescence won last time out and is quickly back in action 14 days later, but she ranks eighth of ten on our figures and that ninth three starts back hints at inconsistency — distance and going experience offer some small comfort, though she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's five-year-old mare is nine days since her last run and races prominently — two runs in similar ground produced no wins or places, and while the prominent style suits the race shape, her recent form string of 542600 suggests she is out of form at present.

races.paceDynamic: Jm Jungle is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger likely to dispute the lead aggressively, he should be able to set his own rhythm down the Beverley five-furlong straight on heavy ground. That said, this field is packed with genuine prominent types — Washington Heights, Shagraan, Heavenly Heather, Al Shabab Storm, Badri, Argentine Tango, and Fluorescence all want to be close to the pace, meaning several will be shuffled back from their natural positions and forced to race in an uncharacteristic midfield berth. The race shape is therefore likely to be a sustainable, controlled gallop set by Jm Jungle, with a wall of prominent types tracking him and jostling for position behind, rather than a truly contested or pressured early pace. On heavy ground over a flat five furlongs with a single honest pace-setter dictating from the front, this race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the testing conditions — hold-up types face a stiff ask to make up ground, and those forced widest in the prominent group will use extra energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jm Jungle sets a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent horses immediately behind him travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: On heavy ground the ability to race within a length or two of the leader without expending early energy proves decisive, with the winner coming from the group that tracks Jm Jungle in the first two or three; Beverley's flat five furlongs rewards horses that can sustain a strong cruising speed rather than those needing a late injection of pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Jm Jungle is allowed to control the tempo entirely unchallenged and the heavy ground turns the race into a test of stamina rather than speed.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied early, Jm Jungle can conserve enough energy to grind out the final furlong as rivals struggle through the mud behind him; his course form and ability to dominate from the front become his greatest asset in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected due to prominent horses squeezing forward at the break and the field burns itself out before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Heavy ground punishes any horse that over-races in the first two furlongs, and if the prominent group fractures and tightens up early, a well-rated hold-up type can pick up the pieces late; Elegant Erin's proven ability to finish off races in testing conditions makes her a logical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Grab Spots
scenarios.trigger: If several of the displaced prominent horses break sharply and manage to reclaim their natural position near the pace, turning the race into a genuinely contested affair.
scenarios.body: With Al Shabab Storm, Badri, or Argentine Tango forcing their way to prominent berths, the early tempo quickens and the race becomes a war of attrition from the halfway point; whichever of those horses handles the heavy going best and conserves most through the first two furlongs stands to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Washington Heights and Shagraan are both natural prominent types with legitimate claims to track Jm Jungle — watch whether they can secure the rail or a clean position in the first furlong, as whichever settles best into second or third is likely to dictate the finish.

Al Shabab Storm, Badri, and Argentine Tango are all genuine prominent racers who cannot all get their position — watch the first half-furlong for crowding and bumping on the inside as this group tries to push forward simultaneously.

Jm Jungle's front-running role is uncontested on paper, but if he goes too conservatively on heavy ground he risks being swallowed up late — watch his early sectional to judge whether he is truly controlling or merely drifting in front.

Elegant Erin and Ain't Nobody are the only genuine hold-up types in the race — watch whether they find clear daylight entering the final furlong, as any pocket trouble in a tightly grouped field on heavy ground will end their challenge immediately.

Beaujolais Nouveau is the lowest-rated runner in the field and ran exclusively over six furlongs in her last five starts — watch for any signs she is used as a pacemaker or that connections are simply using this as a fitness run before her main targets.

races.name: Churchill Tyres EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race; Tim Easterby's David Allan-ridden filly has her best heavy-going chance at this trip and can exploit a complete absence of pace pressure, though OR 60 and a form string showing no win in six starts raises stamina and class doubts late.

runners_data.name: Dawn's Gift
runners_data.note: OR 120 debutant for Sara Ender with only one run to reference (sixth on good); a genuine hold-up operator whose natural game is compromised here because the field is stacked with closers, and she will likely race closer to the pace than suits her best.

runners_data.name: Dorothea Hope
runners_data.note: Easterby's filly has shown gradual improvement across three runs (4-5-8 reversed chronologically), handles good ground fine, but her instinct is to come from off the pace — in a race already crowded at the rear, she must race in a position that is not her own.

runners_data.name: Eleven Eighty Two
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's consistent filly has placed twice at six furlongs on good ground and drops back to five on much softer going for the first time; her prominent style is well-suited to tracking Cheeky Chesca and she is the most naturally positioned horse to challenge the leader.

runners_data.name: Floral Maid
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison debutant with no racecourse evidence and unknown going/style profile; Ellison's yard is 1/17 in the 14-day window, which tempers expectations, but first-time-out fillies on heavy ground at this track are worth monitoring in the market.

runners_data.name: Get On That Baby
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby first-timer for Joanna Mason; completely unexposed, no stylistic data, and the yard's 3/34 14-day strike rate is modest — needs the market to give any steer on confidence levels.

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams filly ran just seven days ago and has a mixed form string including a second and a third at six furlongs; her natural back-of-the-field approach is squeezed in this shape, meaning she is asked to race up with horses she would normally chase down, blunting her late-run threat.

runners_data.name: Picnic Princess
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey debutant for Shane Gray; Fahey's yard is in good form (7/47 over 14 days) and regularly targets maiden fillies' races with well-prepared first-timers — one to watch in the betting.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Voyage
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's Tom Eaves-ridden debutant with no form data; Ryan fires his juveniles out ready and has 3/32 recent runners, which is workmanlike, but unknown style means she could land anywhere in the field map.

runners_data.name: Pocket Change
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's filly returns after 126 days off the track, ran eighth on good ground at five furlongs on debut, and is tagged as a fader — the heavy going and long absence stack against her finding significant improvement here.

runners_data.name: Purrista
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's filly runs just four days after her last start and has been placed (third) once in three runs, all on good ground; a natural hold-up operator who will likely race closer than ideal, and the rapid turnaround on very testing going is a concern.

runners_data.name: Serenity Bay
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's filly has a worrying form profile — faded in her last two starts and ran over seven furlongs on good/soft — dropping back to five on heavy ground for Oisin Orr looks like a significant ask, and the staying-on style she needs is compromised by the sharp trip.

runners_data.name: Suenicora Star
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's second runner (alongside Floral Maid) has two runs behind her including a fifth on good ground at five furlongs; a hold-up operator with modest form who faces the same positional squeeze as the other natural closers in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Cheeky Chesca is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field on heavy ground at Beverley's five-furlong straight, and with no genuine rival to press her for the lead she can dictate a controlled, stamina-sapping gallop from the gates. The heavy going will compress the tempo relative to good ground, making every furlong a war of attrition and rewarding horses who travel well within themselves early rather than those forced wide or back against their instincts. Dawn's Gift, Last Dandelion, and Dorothea Hope are all natural hold-up types redistributed into the midfield picture because genuine back-markers are over-represented in this field, meaning their true closer's game is compromised from the outset. This race shape — one controlled front-runner, a grinding heavy surface, and a field full of horses forced to race closer than they'd like — strongly favours prominent trackers who can sit a length or two off Cheeky Chesca's shoulder and pounce in the final furlong, or unexposed debutants with the raw class to overpower the conditions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cheeky Chesca Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cheeky Chesca breaks cleanly and is allowed to stride clear at a self-selected tempo on heavy ground with no rival willing to go with her.
scenarios.body: She dictates every fraction, conserves energy through the testing surface, and simply needs enough stamina and class to hold on up the straight; her heavy-ground form marker (OK) and sole front-runner status make this the dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Reels Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Cheeky Chesca sets a pace that is just fast enough to tire her out, allowing a close-tracking prominent type to overhaul her in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Eleven Eighty Two, who has a clear prominence profile and consistent placed form, is ideally placed to sit second or third and grind past a flagging leader on the demanding surface; the heavy going rewards those who finish strongest rather than those who simply lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed first-time-out runners (Pivotal Voyage, Picnic Princess, Get On That Baby, or Floral Maid) possesses undetected class that renders the going and race shape irrelevant.
scenarios.body: Trainers Kevin Ryan and Richard Fahey regularly produce sharp debutants on testing ground, and a raw talent breaking cleanly could slot into a prominent position and swamp the field before the placed horses organise; heavy going on a flat five furlongs suits a powerful natural galloper with no form baggage to unravel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and the entire field slows to a crawl, allowing redistributed hold-up types to eventually pick their way through beaten horses late.
scenarios.body: Dawn's Gift or Purrista could theoretically finish fastest of all if the race turns into a stamina test of attrition from the two-furlong pole, but because these hold-up runners are forced to race closer than their natural style demands, their closing kick is diluted and this outcome requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Eleven Eighty Two is the horse most likely to track Cheeky Chesca and overhaul her late — watch whether Andrew Mullen slots her into second spot immediately and whether she handles the drop to five furlongs on heavy ground.

The Fahey and Kevin Ryan debutants (Picnic Princess, Pivotal Voyage) should be monitored for market support drifting in before the off — either yard landing a well-backed newcomer on heavy ground would fundamentally change the race shape assessment.

Purrista runs just four days after her last outing; watch whether her handlers have applied any headgear change or if she shows signs of fatigue in the parade ring, as the rapid turnaround on very testing going is a genuine welfare and performance concern.

With three redistributed hold-up types (Dawn's Gift, Last Dandelion, Dorothea Hope) all forced to race closer than natural on a five-furlong straight, watch the first two furlongs for a bunching incident — congestion behind Cheeky Chesca on heavy ground could cause trouble in running for several runners simultaneously.
Cheeky Chesca's draw and early break will be critical — if she misses the kick or is squeezed at the start, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes genuinely open for the first time.

races.name: Ward Homes Yorkshire Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Golden Redemption
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Harker and Nolan, last five runs all at 6-7f on Good ground — this 1m½f Heavy trip represents a clear query on both stamina and going; 57 days off the track adds another unknown.
runners_data.comment: Golden Redemption showed promise with a second three starts back and a pair of thirds before that, but back-to-back disappointing finishes of seventh and eighth in recent starts are a concern, and he returns winless after 57 days off carrying 132 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Count Palatine
runners_data.note: Won on Soft last time out at 7f, has placed on soft/good-to-soft in similar company, and arrives fresh on 11 days — Michael Dods' 4-from-23 T14 record in handicaps is respectable, and this is the most directly proven horse in the field for these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Count Palatine won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but a sixth two starts back and unplaced efforts elsewhere in recent starts temper enthusiasm; 131 lb from stall 10 is no help either.

runners_data.name: On The River
runners_data.note: Strong Heavy-going record (10 from 15 similar-going starts, 1 win, 3 placed) gives this seven-year-old genuine credentials here, but his natural style is late-running and the crowded hold-up berths mean he will likely be closer than ideal — temper confidence accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, On The River nonetheless brings solid placed form and has run over today's trip and going, with a rating of 86 lending substance to his claims; the worry is whether he can convert consistency into a win when it matters most.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pacemakers; won at 8f on Good but has just one similar-going start from 15, making his stamina and ability to sustain the lead on Heavy ground over 1m½f a significant question mark — headgear worn.
runners_data.comment: Highland Olly won three starts back but has since finished seventh and fifth, and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures he looks hard to fancy at the weights; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 18 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Two wins at 8f on Good recently suggests the form is good, but his heavy-ground exposure is minimal (1 from 15 similar-going) and he is a hold-up type who will need the pace to collapse ahead of him; Sam James takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Priapos has run over today's trip and going, and back-to-back wins four and three starts back show he can produce on his day, but consecutive unplaced efforts since then raise questions, and our rating of 82 leaves him with something to prove at 135 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a fade flag in the finish, which is a genuine concern on Heavy ground over a staying trip — went 5/8/13 in his last three and has no wins on soft or heavy, making this ground profile a material worry.
runners_data.comment: Nostrum heads the ratings here and his speed figure of 88 underlines his claims, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the concern is a winless run of six recent starts that includes two unplaced efforts to close.

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: Six runs on similar going with one win and four placed finishes suggest he handles conditions, but his last five have all been in the 7-8 placed range at this level — O'Meara's 3-from-39 T14 strike rate offers little trainer-form support right now.
runners_data.comment: Walsingham won six starts back, but that victory gives him a fitness edge at 22 days off, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 134 lb from stall 12, he has the conditions in his favour despite a modest run of form since.

runners_data.name: Hot Cash
runners_data.note: Prominent type who placed twice on Soft, handles cut in the ground, and is close enough to peak fitness on 36 days — Channon's 2-from-22 T14 record is modest, and this front-heavy race shape may leave him stranded if pace is brutal.
runners_data.comment: Hot Cash shaped with real promise when finishing second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going gives him a strong each-way profile from stall 11; the main concern is his winless run of form in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Tele Red
runners_data.note: Carries solid form in soft and soft-heavy conditions with 7 from 15 similar-going runs including a win on Soft over 10f — 310 days off the track is the single biggest question mark, and at nine years old the bounce risk after such a layoff is real.
runners_data.comment: Tele Red won two starts back and has been placed in three of his other four recent runs, but 310 days off the track is a significant concern; he has experience of today's trip and going, and his 85 rating suggests ability, though that lengthy absence makes him hard to trust fully.

runners_data.name: Wondrous Light
runners_data.note: Three wins from six similar-going starts, all at 8f on Soft or Soft-to-Standard — Kevin Stott rides a horse with the best heavy/soft strike rate in the field among the prominent types, and 80 days off simply needs a fitness question answered.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and returning from an 80-day absence, Wondrous Light is hard to fancy despite her two wins in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going before, but a speed rating of 66 leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Won last time and is in career-best form, but all wins come on Good or faster — her one soft-going start was a sixth, so this Heavy surface is an unproven variable; headgear worn and Loughnane's 0-from-12 T14 record offers no trainer momentum.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Won at 10f and placed at 9-10f on Good; genuine hold-up horse by preference but the crowded back half of the field means he is likely to find himself in midfield, racing out of his most effective role — limited heavy-going exposure (2 from 15) also tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Financer has found only one winner in his last six starts, and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures he faces a stiff task here, though second last time out shows he retains some form and he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Panelli
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner alongside Highland Olly; headgear worn and two placed efforts on Standard at 7-8f, but no meaningful evidence of heavy-ground or staying-trip effectiveness, with just one similar-going start — if Highland Olly takes it up, Panelli may be the first to capitulate.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Panelli is hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going; the seventh last time out is the most recent evidence, and 118 lb from stall 13 adds little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly and Panelli are the two confirmed front-runners and will fight for the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested pace on testing Heavy ground over 1m½f at Beverley — the gallop will be honest rather than suicidal, but the energy expenditure on this surface will be significant. Count Palatine and Hot Cash will push forward to prominent positions, while Wondrous Light and The Sweet Escape add further pressure in the first half of the field, meaning the front of the race will be crowded and competitive throughout. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — On The River and Financer are genuine late-runners by preference but are shown in midfield because Nostrum, Priapos, Walsingham, and Golden Redemption fill the natural hold-up berths; On The River and Financer are unlikely to settle as deep as they would wish. The contested early fractions on extreme Heavy ground over this longer trip will drain the leaders and prominent racers, and the race shape strongly favours horses with proven stamina in soft/heavy conditions who can deliver a sustained finish from midfield or a true hold-up position — classically suited to the genuine closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Past Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly and Panelli set a true pace that burns the prominent brigade in the Heavy ground, allowing genuine hold-up horses to pick them off.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners cut out real work on an energy-sapping surface, and horses held up off the pace conserve enough to sustain their runs into the straight; the longer trip amplifies the stamina premium and rewards those who travel smoothly in rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stays On Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not brutal, leaving one of the prominent types with enough reserves to outstay rivals through the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Count Palatine brings solid soft-ground form and recent race fitness, while Wondrous Light has multiple wins on soft surfaces and handles the trip; either can sustain a prominent run if the pace is judged well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies Logic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is miscalculated and only one of the two front-runners commits fully, allowing the other to dictate at a surprisingly moderate tempo.
scenarios.body: Heavy ground at Beverley can produce surprisingly low fractions if one front-runner folds early and leaves the other with a soft lead; Highland Olly, who has a win at 8f on Good, would need a soft enough lead to conserve energy, but Panelli has headgear and similar course maps making this unlikely but not impossible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough for a well-positioned midfield horse to produce a well-timed run and find a gap as leaders tire.
scenarios.body: Financer and On The River, though redistributed from their natural hold-up roles, may find themselves in a workable midfield position if traffic shapes favourably in the straight; their style-fit discount means this is the least reliable shape, but the longer trip gives them a window.

watchPoints.text: Highland Olly and Panelli will fight each other for the lead — watch the first two furlongs to see which of the two dictates, because if neither backs off the pair could burn excessive energy that collapses the front half of the race.

Count Palatine is the most proven horse for this exact going profile and arrives on a sharp 11-day turnaround with a recent Soft-ground win — if he slots prominently behind the front two he becomes the most dangerous live rival.

Tele Red returns from a 310-day absence and, despite strong soft-ground form, the fitness question on this extreme surface over 1m½f is severe — watch the betting market as a proxy for confidence; if drifting sharply, discount heavily.

Wondrous Light carries the best similar-going win percentage among prominent types but has been off 80 days — an absence flag combined with a strong profile means his market move pre-race is the key read.

On The River and Financer are true hold-up horses who will likely race closer than ideal given the congested rear — watch how much they can detach in the straight; if they are stuck wide or behind a wall of horses, their chances diminish sharply.

races.name: Constant Security Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a clear lead role here; Paul McDonald takes over and Geoff Oldroyd has a runner fit and fresh at 16 days; the sole heavy-ground win came in a much smaller field and sim-going figures (1/9, no wins) temper confidence, but position on paper is unassailable.

runners_data.name: Holbache
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old campaigner with strong course form and a headgear flag suggesting connections are trying to sharpen him; Julie Camacho's yard is 0/15 in the past fortnight, and recent runs on good ground show consistent prominence without converting — heavy ground at Beverley is a concern on the sim-going (5/15) data.
runners_data.comment: Holbache has won in his last five starts but two latest efforts were an eighth and a fifth, and ranked twelfth of fourteen on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 17 days since his last outing suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Military Girl
runners_data.note: Michael Dods sends her in good recent form (1-1-2-3 in last five on good), trained actively with 4/23 in 14 days and Connor Beasley takes the ride; no sim-going wins but has placed twice in 15 visits to similar ground, making her the most consistent prominent racer in the field on evidence.
runners_data.comment: Military Girl shaped well when runner-up two starts back and has run over today's trip and going before, with our rating of 78 marking her out as a leading contender; the main concern is that fifth last time out, which raises a question over consistency.

runners_data.name: Daizen
runners_data.note: Only three years old and already showing prominently — won over 6f on good but sim-going is 6/12, a concern; Andrew Mullen retains the ride and Rebecca Menzies is 1/17 over the fortnight, so this looks more of a handicapper finding its level than a standout contender in conditions.
runners_data.comment: Daizen won three starts back but has been out of the placings in both runs since, and nine days between starts is a quick turnaround; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a mark of 73 leaves some room, though recent form makes him a hold-your-breath each-way proposition from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up specialist for Paul Midgley who has run consistently without winning in 2024; sim-going data (4/15) suggests he handles these conditions better than most rivals and David Nolan is a positive booking, though his finishing kick on heavy turf is modest.
runners_data.comment: Ventura Express heads this field on ratings and has run over today's trip and going before, giving connections every reason for optimism; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, suggesting the winning moment remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Qila
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type with headgear (t), placed twice in similar going sim-data (2/6); Brian Ellison's runner is lightly raced at 5f and the jockey booking of M.P. Sheehy is unfamiliar — has ability but may be undone by the prominent traffic battle given inexperience.
runners_data.comment: Qila has shown consistency without a win in recent starts, posting thirds last time out and two starts back, though the trainer's current 5% strike rate over the past fortnight is a concern carrying 134 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Tiriac
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Paul Midgley (same stable as Ventura Express), fitted with headgear (p) and returning at 29 days; sim-going of 5/15 and recent form string of 978056 tells its own story — part of the midfield cluster with limited upside on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Tiriac nevertheless catches the eye on conditions, having run over today's distance and going before, and he steps back up in fitness terms after 29 days off; carrying 134 lb from stall four, his speed rating of 79 gives him scope to outrun his official mark of 69.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Recent form of 331700 is patchy and sim-going (2/15) shows two placed efforts but no wins in similar conditions; Jack Nicholls (3) claims 3lb which is useful in a handicap, and the 13-day return means he is fit, though the form drop to 0 last time is a red flag.
runners_data.comment: Tees Aggregates has run over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back offers encouragement, but two unplaced efforts and a seventh in his last three runs — including two back-to-back — are a concern, and he faces a stiff ask from stall 10 carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Sam England's four-year-old has won twice on good ground and placed on soft in the sim-going sample; Shane Gray takes the ride and the trainer is 3/12 in the last fortnight — no heavy-ground data makes this a harder case to assess but the recent form figures (715317) show it can win at this level.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Great is hard to fancy off a seventh last time out, and only one win in his last four starts adds little confidence; that said, he has run over today's trip before and comes here on a sound 19-day break.

runners_data.name: Miss Brazen
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby runner with a genuine preference for racing behind the pace, though the crowded map has pushed her into a midfield position she would not naturally seek; best run recently was a third on good ground, and the trainer's 3/34 strike rate over the fortnight is low — style fit is compromised in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Miss Brazen showed she could win, doing so five starts back, but four runs without troubling the judge since leave her with plenty to prove; she has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 72 gives her a slim edge over her official mark.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Michael Dods (same yard as Military Girl), running from OR 68 with recent form of 154347 — the 1 and 5 in that string show some ability; Mark Winn takes the ride and the horse lacks heavy-ground data, making this a speculative entry in a prominent-heavy field.
runners_data.comment: Ran a creditable third three starts back but has since slipped to a seventh last time out, so consistency is the question mark; he has run over today's trip and a 72 rating suggests a shade of ability, though 131 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ice Cold Alex
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears horse with a headgear flag (p) who is a natural hold-up type shuffled into midfield on this map due to the rear-of-field congestion; sim-going (3/10) gives some confidence in conditions, but racing closer than ideal and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 tempers expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ice Cold Alex nonetheless has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and his 10-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh; the 130 lb burden may be the chief obstacle to reversing recent unplaced efforts.

runners_data.name: Empress Olivia
runners_data.note: Mark Walford three-year-old with 0/8 for the trainer in the fortnight and a modest sim-going record (3/13 with one win); Dougie Costello is a quality booking but the form string of 104067 shows a big drop recently and the 33-day absence adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Empress Olivia scored within her last six starts and our rating of 77 rates her a serious threat from stall 2 carrying 129 lb, with experience of today's trip and going in her favour; the worry is that she has been out of the placings in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old is naturally prominent-minded but has been nudged into midfield on the map because there is no room up front for another prominent runner; David Allan rides and the horse has placed twice on similar going, but STYLE_FIT at 0.93 means finishing closest to its best requires a scenario where it actually travels prominently — not guaranteed in a 15-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Dream Deal ranks last on our figures among the 14 runners, and an unplaced effort heading into today makes him hard to fancy, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and stall one is his draw.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's seven-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield; Jason Hart rides and the 9-day turnaround shows the yard has it ready, with sim-going (2/15, one place) giving some confidence; style is most compromised in this race shape and the STYLE_FIT penalty of 0.92 reflects that reality.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Harb faces a stiff ask here, though he was second last time out and has run over today's distance and going before, offering slim but genuine grounds for optimism.

races.paceDynamic: Managing Director is the lone confirmed front-runner and, critically, faces no genuine rival for the lead — the prominent cluster of Holbache, Military Girl, Daizen, Qila, and Simba's Pride will jostle hard in the first furlong to secure positions just behind, creating a fast-tempo scramble through the early stages on heavy ground that will test stamina rather than pure speed. That prominent congestion between the 2f and 3f markers is the defining tactical hazard of this race, with six horses all wanting a similar position but only space for two or three to travel comfortably. Dream Deal, Miss Brazen, Ice Cold Alex, and Harb are true prominent or hold-up types who have been pushed back on the map because there is simply no room at the front; of those, Dream Deal is most likely to find a position closer to the action given connections' intent, while Managing Director is best placed to dictate from the front unopposed. In heavy ground over 5f at Beverley, the race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel prominently without burning energy in the early scramble and hit the rising finish with something in reserve — a well-positioned prominent or front-runner who avoids the traffic is the profile to side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Managing Director dictates a sustainable gallop unchallenged and the prominent pack fails to close the gap up the Beverley rise.
scenarios.body: Managing Director bowls along on a flat track in heavy ground, setting an honest but measured tempo that is within his comfort zone, and the prominent horses behind him burn energy scrapping for position rather than attacking the leader; the rising finish then stretches the field and rewards the horse who has conserved most energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle for positions 2-5 creates a fast early pace that burns off front-runners and leaves the field to be picked off.
scenarios.body: The early jostling among Holbache, Daizen, Military Girl, and Qila forces a strong tempo that drains those prominent horses entering the final furlong; runners who have managed to travel smoothly just off the pace without getting shuffled around then finish strongest on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield becomes gridlocked between 2f and 3f out, leaving true hold-up types with a clear late run.
scenarios.body: With 15 runners on heavy ground and prominent congestion causing a logjam in the mid-race, a horse that drops out early and finds a clear route up the outer in the final furlong could benefit from a clear passage when others are bunched; however, Miss Brazen, Ice Cold Alex, and Harb are all racing somewhat out of their preferred roles having been pushed back, reducing the likelihood this shape truly delivers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Strolls
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses concede too much ground to Managing Director through caution after the early scrimmage, leaving the leader unopposed to slow the race and sprint clear.
scenarios.body: An unusually modest tempo — surprising given the size of field but possible if the prominent runners over-race and then back off — would suit a horse with sharp acceleration who can track a slow pace and quicken; on heavy ground this is the least likely shape as the going negates pure finishing speed.

watchPoints.text: Managing Director leads but 15 runners in heavy ground means the prominent pack (Holbache, Military Girl, Daizen, Qila) will surge hard to sit behind — watch for crowding in the first furlong that disrupts the leader's rhythm.

The 2f–3f marker is the critical flashpoint: six prominent types competing for three or four positions will cause traffic chaos in midfield, with Dream Deal and Ice Cold Alex particularly vulnerable to being squeezed out of their preferred spots.

Heavy ground at Beverley (confirmed across all seven races today) will significantly stretch finishing times — any horse that over-races in the prominent battle early is likely to stop sharply on the rise to the line, making early position decisions decisive.

Ventura Express and Tiriac are both hold-up types from the same Paul Midgley yard; if they race in tandem and one gets boxed in behind the midfield logjam, stable tactics could become a complicating factor in the straight.

Miss Brazen and Harb are both racing further forward than their natural role — if either gets shuffled wider in the straight away from the midfield traffic, a wider berth could accidentally become a race-saving advantage in the final furlong.

races.name: Return Of The Legend Martin Spencer Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Printing Money
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Dylan Cunha, running 11 days ago over 7f at Sandown; tongue-tie and hood in play, but zero wins from four starts and no sim-going form makes the heavy surface a genuine unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Printing Money has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround of just 11 days, with our rating of 72 marking him out as the one to beat in this field; yet to win in his last four starts, though that third last time out suggests he is knocking on the door.

runners_data.name: Nosey Book
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's prominent racer has placed at 7f on good for Sean Kirrane and steps back to a slightly shorter trip; the yard is in solid form at 4/71 and blinkers could sharpen his early pace.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Nosey Book does return with experience over today's trip and a quick 15-day turnaround in his favour, though a third two starts back is his sole recent encouragement and he faces a stiff task from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Sunrise At Dawn
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's runner is a natural hold-up horse whose sole similar-going win came at 6f — a true rear-of-field type who is likely to find himself further forward than ideal given the field's depth of closers; the step up to 7½f heavy is also new territory.|
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out but winless in her last four starts, Sunrise At Dawn has the fitness question of 46 days off to answer; draw three and a solid speed rating offer some encouragement, though her rating of 62 suggests she holds her own in this company.

runners_data.name: Black Fury
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners this Ollie Pears prominent racer who has been placed at 8f on good, suggesting the trip and stamina are assets; handles a stiff test and the heavy could amplify his staying power rather than blunt it.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Black Fury faces a stiff task here; second last time out is the one bright note, and she has run over today's trip before, but the weight of 126 lb from stall ten adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Inns And Out
runners_data.note: David Allan rides this Tim Easterby hold-up horse who has won at 7f on good just five days ago, making the quick turnaround the key query; form is progressive and the victory suggests class enough to cope, but freshness must be monitored.|
runners_data.comment: Inns And Out arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, with his rating of 66 ranking him second of these and marking him a strong threat; the main concern is just five days between runs, which may leave him short of peak freshness.

runners_data.name: Bella Lucia
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter; Gemma Tutty's filly won at 7f on good and has placed twice, but her STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she'll be running further forward than optimal given her best form pattern — the lone lead is an opportunity, not a guaranteed platform.|
runners_data.comment: Bella Lucia comes into this in good heart after winning last time out, though a sixth three starts back tempers expectations; she has run over today's trip and returns after 23 days, carrying 135 lb from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's hold-up performer has been in consistent form across six runs (123351) with a 7f win on good and sim-going data showing no wins from ten similar-ground starts; the form profile is strong but the heavy surface is a significant stamina query despite the step up in trip.|
runners_data.comment: Amantha advertises her claims with a win last time out and has run over today's trip, while her 132 lb burden from stall 11 underlines her quality — the chief worry is a trainer operating at just five per cent in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Court Legend
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's hold-up runner wears a hood and ran second over 8f on good last time; the Easterby yard is active, but two runs out of the frame at 6f prior suggest the extra distance is needed — interesting if the trip suits.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in recent starts, Court Legend was a close second last time out and returns here in solid shape just 17 days later; he has run over today's trip and our rating of 66 marks him out as a genuine threat, though he remains winless and will need to find more to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Dynasty
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's fader is tagged as a true hold-up horse mapped forward due to redistribution — all three career runs have ended in the bottom half of the field, and the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag alongside the style-fit discount makes this a speculative foray at best.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of eighths and a seventh in recent outings, Scarlet Dynasty is hard to fancy on these figures despite carrying just 121 lb from stall one and having experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type from Tim Easterby's powerful yard who has placed at 7f and 8f on good, wearing headgear; the redistribution means he is unlikely to get his preferred last-of-all berth, and with 30 days off the freshness factor is uncertain.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Tiger In The Tree does at least bring distance experience and a return from a 30-day break that should leave her fresh, though her rating of 56 and a draw of nine from 12 suggest she faces a stiff task to improve on consecutive thirds.

runners_data.name: Be More Ruthless
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls's prominent runner holds a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag across three unplaced starts; Jack Nicholls takes the 3lb claim but heavy ground over 7½f looks beyond a horse yet to reach the frame.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Be More Ruthless faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and returns on a workable 18-day break, but little else in her recent profile invites confidence.

runners_data.name: Loveulongtime
runners_data.note: Geoffrey Harker's prominent runner for William Pyle has form figures of 7048 and has not threatened at any of four outings; the step up to 7½f on heavy is entirely unexplored territory and there is no evidence of improvement needed to factor here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Loveulongtime faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip before and her 18-day turnaround suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Bella Lucia is the confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should stride out uncontested to set a sustainable rather than suicidal gallop on heavy ground at Beverley's 7½f. Nosey Book and Black Fury will press from just off the pace in a prominent berth, while the hold-up brigade — Printing Money, Inns And Out, Amantha, and Court Legend — will be settled in the rear third. The field actually contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the back: Sunrise At Dawn, Tiger In The Tree, and Scarlet Dynasty are genuine closers who are likely to find themselves shuffled into mid-division rather than their natural last position, meaning their finishing kicks will be diluted by a more forward starting point. On heavy ground over 7½f at Beverley, a controlled lead with a single front-runner setting an honest but unforced tempo is the scenario most likely to play out, and the profile that benefits most is a resolute hold-up or late-prominent runner with proven stamina, ideally one who has won or placed on similar conditions — not a horse dependent on a true end-to-end test to make an impact.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bella Lucia Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Lucia dictates a measured pace from the front and the prominent horses cannot sustain a challenge through the deep ground.
scenarios.body: Bella Lucia pings the gate under Conor Whiteley and sets a controlled rhythm that leaves the hold-up horses with too much ground to make up; the heavy going rewards her stamina and her rivals' finishing runs are blunted.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Lucia's solo lead produces a slightly too-strong early clip and the hold-up horses find a clear passage to close powerfully in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The deep ground ultimately tells on the front-runner in the closing stages and a genuine stayer pressing from mid-division picks her off; Inns And Out's recent winning form at 7f on good and Amantha's consistency over 7f make them the most likely beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Run On
scenarios.trigger: If Nosey Book or Black Fury track Bella Lucia at close quarters and prove strong enough to collar her as she tires in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This shape requires one of the prominent duo to simply outstay the leader rather than produce a turn of foot, which is plausible on heavy ground; Black Fury's placed run at 8f on good suggests he stays and could grind past a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the horses naturally inclined to race at the rear — Sunrise At Dawn, Tiger In The Tree, Scarlet Dynasty — somehow secure a truly wide berth and produce a late swoop.
scenarios.body: This scenario is markedly discounted because all three are tagged as redistibuted hold-up types who are unlikely to get their natural position, negating their best form; even if one does close late, their style-fit in this shape is compromised and the heavy ground demands earlier engagement.

watchPoints.text: Bella Lucia's lead — if she bowls along unchallenged and the race lacks a genuine pursuer to honest the pace, the closers may never generate enough momentum on heavy ground to reach her; watch whether Nosey Book or Black Fury press forward to force genuine early tempo.

Inns And Out ran just five days ago and wins must be weighed against that rapid turnaround — if David Allan finds the horse below his peak, the yard's prolific run-rate becomes a double-edged sword in heavy conditions.

The group of redistributed hold-up horses (Sunrise At Dawn, Tiger In The Tree, Scarlet Dynasty) will be jostling for position mid-division rather than settling at the rear; watch for the early stages to become congested in the middle of the field as these horses are forced wider and earlier than suits.

Amantha's sim-going record (0 wins from 10 runs on similar going) is notable for a horse with otherwise strong form — if the heavy surface proves her undoing, the scenario shifts significantly toward Bella Lucia holding on or the prominent pair running on.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Southwell in latest run and has finished in the frame over 15f in similar heavy-ish conditions; natural hold-up style is perfectly suited to chasing down a lone leader in the straight, and the 55-day break with Iain Jardine's 2/19 record over 14 days is not alarming given the horse clearly needs a target to aim at.
runners_data.comment: Elemental Eye shaped with real promise when second last time out, and a winner two starts back, showing he handles today's distance and going; a 55-day absence is the only query, but his rating of 72 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Marbuzet
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type with solid 2m+ form at Goodwood and Sandown but the sim-going record of 0 wins from 1 run on genuinely soft/heavy is a question mark; the 5lb claim of Jake Dickson helps at the weights and Tim Easterby's 4/71 trainer strike rate over 14 days is workmanlike rather than exciting.
runners_data.comment: Marbuzet has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him second among eight here, suggesting he is well-equipped to mount a strong challenge; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with a ninth last time out the immediate worry.

runners_data.name: Time Turner
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by inclination — Edward Bethell's runner will want to race last and pounce, but with so many rivals sharing that instinct, Cian Horgan's 3lb claim may see him forced to race more prominently than ideal, and the STYLE_FIT penalty of 0.94 reflects a meaningful positional compromise over 2m on heavy.
runners_data.comment: Time Turner has hit the frame in two of his last three starts, including a second two starts back and a third last time out, and he has experience over today's trip — the main question is whether 135 lb blunts his chance.

runners_data.name: Pfingstberg
runners_data.note: Back after a remarkable 696-day absence for Mark Walford, who also saddles the leader; won twice over 16f at Southwell including a recent win and placed over 14f at Sandown, so the trip and likely surface are fine, but the layoff is a massive fitness caveat and the trainer's 0/8 14-day record offers no confidence of a well-laid return.
runners_data.comment: An absence of nearly two years makes Pfingstberg very hard to assess on fitness alone, and he ranks seventh of eight on our figures, yet he has run over today's trip and going before and boasts two wins in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Shopaholic
runners_data.note: Form figures of 3-2 in his last two runs over 13-14f at Sandown suggest he's in good heart, but his instinct is to race off the pace and the redistribution note reveals he'll be pushed forward against his grain; Jack Jones's 1/11 14-day record is modest and the 0/5 sim-going record on similar surfaces tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but has placed on two of her three most recent outings, and 22 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; the weight of 134 lb is a stern burden, however, that may blunt her chances of converting that consistency into something more.

runners_data.name: Spooky Wooky
runners_data.note: Placed in his last run at Goodwood over 14f on good-to-firm and has decent soft-ground placed efforts at 15-16f, suggesting the trip and conditions aren't alien; however, this horse naturally wants to race last and will find himself operating further forward than he'd like with so many rivals sharing the same instinct — a secondary concern behind the fitness of the front two.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Spooky Wooky at least has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a fourth last time out and a seventh two starts back leave his form looking modest heading in.

runners_data.name: Punxsutawney Phil
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from flag to finish, but 527 days off the track is a serious fitness red flag even if Mark Walford has placed him here deliberately; won over 20f on soft and has multiple placed efforts around that trip, so the distance is right, but his sim-going record of 9/15 runs suggests heavy is not his favoured terrain and his ability to sustain the lead for 2m in this state is questionable.
runners_data.comment: Punxsutawney Phil's experience over today's distance and going is a genuine asset, and a rating of 70 puts him ahead of the official mark, suggesting he retains ability — though winless in his last five starts and returning after 527 days off, rustiness is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: Raced just 10 days ago so is at least race-fit; hold-up style is his natural mode, blinkered, and the 1 win from 15 runs in sim-going conditions is a fair indicator of his level, but Paul Midgley's 2/10 14-day record is solid and he's shown consistency over 12-13f — stepping to 2m on heavy may simply be beyond him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Jedhi Knight nevertheless shows some consistency — third and second among those runs — and has run over today's trip and going before, but rated 8 of 8 on our figures he faces a stiff task against this field.

races.paceDynamic: Punxsutawney Phil is the sole confirmed front-runner and, returning from 527 days off, will almost certainly bowl along in front unchallenged on heavy ground over 2m at Beverley — a recipe for a solo, economy-pace lead that never gets seriously tested until deep in the home straight. Behind him, Pfingstberg is the only other prominent type, likely to track in second and control the chasing pack, meaning the gallop is set by just two horses with no rival willing or able to press them. The bulk of the field — Elemental Eye, Marbuzet, Time Turner, Shopaholic, Spooky Wooky and Jedhi Knight — are all hold-up horses by nature, though Time Turner, Shopaholic, Spooky Wooky and Jedhi Knight have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all occupy the rear as their natural style demands. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a steady-to-moderate heavy-ground tempo — overwhelmingly favours genuine, proven hold-up types who stay well and can produce a sustained late run, with Elemental Eye and Marbuzet best placed by their natural style to exploit any gap; Pfingstberg, as the closest pursuer throughout, is the dangerous alternative if the pace collapses early enough to reward front-to-back stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Punxsutawney Phil Leads Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the heavy ground slows the race to such a crawl that Phil's rivals simply cannot close the gap he has built over 2m.
scenarios.body: Punxsutawney Phil gets a completely uncontested lead and dictates a plodding tempo that saps the energy from the closers; his rivals burn too much fuel trying to make ground on the testing surface and he holds on grimly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Power Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Punxsutawney Phil sets a genuine, honest pace — even if slow — that stretches the field and the true hold-up horses pick up powerfully in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: The lone leader ensures enough early movement that the genuine stay-all-day hold-up types build momentum on the home turn and the sustained closing run punishes any rival who has over-committed; heavy ground rewards the deepest stayers producing a single relentless surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Pfingstberg, sitting directly behind the leader throughout, presses at the top of the straight and the redistributed midfield horses lack the energy to mount a genuine late challenge.
scenarios.body: Pfingstberg's race position is ideal — saving ground, covered up, never off the bridle — and on a track where getting into the race late can be costly on heavy ground, tracking the leader pays a handsome dividend.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffle Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the heavy ground causes attrition up front and several redistributed hold-up types manage to find a racing line despite being out of their natural role.
scenarios.body: Shopaholic, Spooky Wooky or Jedhi Knight, racing more prominently than they would ideally choose, find themselves in a better position than expected when the front two tire; the style-fit discount still applies but a collapse in front can flatter them.

watchPoints.text: Punxsutawney Phil's fitness after 527 days off is the pivotal factor — if he ties up before the home turn the entire pace map collapses and any horse can win.

Pfingstberg has been absent for 696 days and, while Mark Walford runs both the leader and this tracker, a fitness-compromised Pfingstberg losing ground rounding the home turn would remove the chief threat to the hold-up horses.

Time Turner, Shopaholic, Spooky Wooky and Jedhi Knight are all natural hold-up horses forced into midfield positions by the volume of closers — watch for a bunched, scrimmaging midfield that denies any of them a clean run when the race develops.

Heavy ground at Beverley over 2m late in the card — the going report confirms heavy all day — means stamina doubts for any runner without a proven heavy-ground stay; Marbuzet's single sim-going effort and Shopaholic's limited similar-surface record are worth monitoring in-running.

Apprentice jockeys dominate this field — Dickson (5lb), Horgan (3lb), Tindall (3lb), Whiteley (3lb) and Elliott (3lb) — increasing the chance of positional errors over this marathon trip on testing ground, particularly in the bunched midfield group.
